Objective for processing:  
This work will use breast and cervical screening annual return data ( KC returns) to construct graphical and other methods of analysis to enhance performance evaluation of both breast screening and cervical screening in England, by allowing for confounding factors and statistical ability. This work is a small part of a larger agreement relating to quality assurance in the cancer screening programme (ECM-2319) which is currently funded by Public Health England.
Processing activities: 
Data will be stored at the University of Oxford Cancer Epidemiology Unit (CEU) and only accessed by Dr Roger Blanks (Senior Epidemiologist) and Mr Rupert Alison (Data manager). Data will be analysed using EXCEL and the statistical package STATA. Data will normally be analysed as stand-alone but may be linked with public domain aggregated data (e.g. census data at an equivalent local authority level).
Specific outputs expected, including target date: 
Reports will be presented to the breast and cervical screening evaluation groups. These will be on development of age adjusted and other confounding factor adjusted performance measures.  For example, in cervical screening the APV-PPV graph and referral value measures in cervical screening could be adjusted to a common mean age and for other potential confounding factors to enable better comparison between laboratories.  For some measures there may be potential for peer-reviewed research papers to be written if results are of national or international interest. A number of measures are likely to be developed up to the project contract period which expires in March 2018.
Expected measurable benefits to health and/or social care including target date: 
Previous studies have made major contributions to the performance of screening programmes including substantial increases in sensitivity (circa 30% more invasive cancers detected - see research papers on screening by Blanks RG) from development of standardised detection ratio, work on two view mammography and double film reading and development of the PPV-referral diagram.  Many of the current performance measures being used in both the breast and cervical screening programmes were developed by using and modifying KC return information and combining with additional information where appropriate to maximise programme performance.
Research will be published in journals if appropriate, and where peer-review is desirable.
